name: Build and renew underground plant (cable crews)
summary: Cable crews install and replace underground primary cable, padmount transformers and switchgear, splice and terminate cable after civil contractors have built the ducts and vaults, and energize new subdivisions. An inspector first confirms the civil work is ready, a planner gets the dig points located and an outage booked, and stores stage reels and equipment. A crew of two or three splicers and an apprentice pulls cable, sets equipment, splices, tests and energizes under a work protection permit, then hands back redlines and hours. Jobs stall when contractors are late, when transformers and switchgear are on backorder, and on the multi-address locate and outage notice lead times.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 346,000 customers, 3,167 km of underground line and 14 in-house cable crews.
baseline.notes: Civil work (trenching, boring, ducts, vaults) is done by contractors under other processes; this workflow covers the in-house cable crew's part.

trigger: Work scheduling releases the work order to a cable crew with a planned week (crew schedule).
end_state: Cable and equipment are installed, tested and energized, crew time is approved and the as-built has reached the capital project manager; or the job is deferred.

volume.seasonality: Lower from December to March when frost limits excavation and new subdivisions slow; busiest from June to November.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate kept: about 540 underground work orders a year fits 14 cable crews that also handle cable faults and service connections.

surge.cause: autumn push to energize new subdivisions and finish cable renewal before frost

evidence.note: Builders and capital programs aim to finish before winter; multiplier is the author's estimate.
Organisation file role and loaded cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Four supervisors cover construction, faults and service work.

systems.name: ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Mobile workforce management and field tablets
Document management and engineering drawing repository
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
Ontario One Call member portal and locate management
SCADA for stations and feeder devices
Time entry for crews and staff

resources.name: Underground cable crew (two to three cable splicers with a cable truck)
Cable splicing truck or van with generator
Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Review the released job package
steps.description: The underground supervisor opens the scheduled work order in the ERP and mobile workforce tool, reads the design package (cable routes, duct and vault drawings, splice and termination details, transformer and switchgear specifications) and assigns a crew lead.

error.defect_description: A missing splice detail or wrong cable size is not noticed.

evidence.note: Supervisor review of released jobs; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm the civil work is ready
steps.description: A construction inspector visits the site to confirm the civil contractor has finished: ducts installed and proven with a mandrel, vaults, transformer pads and switchgear bases set at grade, pull strings in place. They record what is missing on the inspection form.

error.defect_description: A blocked or crushed duct is not found until the cable pull.

next.condition: ducts, vaults or pads not finished or deficient
job deferred or merged with another

evidence.note: Contractors build ducts and road crossings before crews replace cable (source); readiness shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the civil contractor to finish
steps.description: The civil contractor completes or repairs the ducts, vaults and pads, often working around other subdivision trades or winter conditions, and notifies the project manager when the site is ready again.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Contractor delays are a known hold-up for cable crews (organisation file); the one to six week range is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit locate requests
steps.description: The work planner enters the excavation points (splice pits, transformer pads, riser poles, road crossings) on the Ontario One Call portal with the planned dig date and files the ticket numbers on the job.

error.defect_description: A dig point is left off the request.

control.basis: Ontario Underground Infrastructure Notification System Act, 2012 and Occupational Health and Safety Act: locate all buried plant before excavating

steps.name: Wait for underground owners to mark the site
steps.description: The utility's own locators and the gas, telecom, water and municipal owners mark their buried plant at each dig point. Owners have five business days for a single address and ten for a multi-address request, which most cable jobs are.

error.defect_description: A buried line is marked in the wrong place or missed.

evidence.note: Ten business days is about two calendar weeks.

steps.name: Stage cable reels and equipment
steps.description: A stores attendant issues cable reels, splice and termination kits, elbows, padmount transformers or switchgear against the work order in the ERP and arranges delivery of reels and transformers to site or to the cable truck.

error.defect_description: Wrong cable size or kit type issued.

next.condition: transformer, switchgear or cable on backorder

evidence.note: Author's estimate; staging runs during the locate window.

steps.name: Chase long-lead equipment
steps.description: The work planner works with the buyer on delivery dates for padmount transformers, switchgear or a specific cable, checks whether an approved substitute is in another job's stock, and moves the job if needed.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Transformer and switchgear lead times lengthened in 2021-2022; share and wait are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request switching and a planned outage
steps.description: The work planner sends the control room a switching request for the tie-in or equipment change, with isolation points, date and protection holder, and asks for planned outage notices for the customers on the affected loop or radial.

error.defect_description: Wrong device or date on the request.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the switching order and book the outage
steps.description: A switching and outage planner checks the underground loop in the GIS and outage management system, writes the switching order and grounding points, books the outage window so customers get advance notice, and triggers the notices.

error.defect_description: Open point or isolation point wrong in the order.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code (IHSA): work protection permit and tags issued by the control room before work on isolated plant

evidence.note: Wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold for the booked crew day and outage window
steps.description: The job waits for the crew slot and the date given to customers in the outage notice. The day before, the supervisor confirms the crew, cable truck, reels, switching order and contractor support.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: customer asks to move the outage, crew pulled to a cable fault, or frozen ground

evidence.note: Outage dates are set days ahead so notices can go out; wait and postponement share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Reschedule the job
steps.description: The work planner rebooks the crew day with the supervisor, moves the switching order and outage with the control room, and has new notices sent.

error.defect_description: Customers not told of the new date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive the crew and cable truck to site
steps.description: The cable crew loads splice kits and elbows and drives the splicing truck, reel trailer and generator from the operations centre to the site, often across the city.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold the tailboard and set up the site
steps.description: The crew lead runs the pre-job briefing and hazard assessment, fences open vaults and excavations, sets up traffic control and checks the gas detector and vault ventilation before anyone enters a vault.

error.defect_description: A hazard is not recorded or discussed.

control.basis: Electrical Utility Safety Rules (IHSA) and Ontario Regulation 213/91: hazard assessment, confined space entry and traffic protection

evidence.note: Share of jobs with a cable pull is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pull new cable into the ducts
steps.description: The crew sets up the reel trailer and winch, attaches the pulling eye to the pull string, lubricates and pulls the cable through the ducts between vaults or pads while watching tension, and leaves enough tail for splicing.

error.defect_description: Jacket damaged or tension exceeded during the pull.

evidence.note: New cable goes in conduit (source); pull time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take work protection from the control room
steps.description: The system operator directs the switching on the loop; the crew opens elbows or switchgear and reports each step. The operator issues the work protection permit, and the protection holder tests the cable dead and applies grounds at both ends.

error.defect_description: Device operated out of order.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code (IHSA): work protection permit and tags issued by the control room before work on isolated plant

next.condition: transformer or switchgear to set or replace

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Set or replace padmount equipment
steps.description: The crew disconnects the old padmount transformer or switchgear, lifts it out with the boom truck, sets the new unit on the pad, and checks rating, phasing and grounding against the drawing.

error.defect_description: Grounding or phasing connected wrong.

evidence.note: Transformer replacement is part of cable renewal (source); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Splice and terminate the cable
steps.description: Two cable splicers prepare cable ends, install splices and load-break elbows at transformers and switchgear, and make terminations at riser poles, following the splice kit instructions and company standards. A 28 kV splice takes a few hours of careful work.

error.defect_description: Splice workmanship defect (contamination, wrong cutback).

evidence.note: Splicing times are the author's estimate from common practice.

steps.name: Prepare cable and assist the splicers
steps.description: The apprentice cleans and trains cable ends, passes tools and kit parts, runs the generator and keeps the vault ventilated and the work zone clear while the splicers work.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: One apprentice per crew, as in the organisation file; runs alongside the splicing.

steps.name: Test the new cable before energizing
steps.description: The crew runs an insulation or very low frequency withstand test on the new section, checks phasing, records results on the test sheet and fixes any failure before handing back.

error.defect_description: Marginal result accepted.

control.basis: Company construction standard: test new primary cable before energizing

next.condition: test fails, splice or termination redone

evidence.note: Test practice and failure rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Inspect the installation
steps.description: A construction inspector checks the installation against the drawings and standards: cable identification, splice locations, grounding, clearances at pads, labels and test records, and records any deficiency.

error.defect_description: A deficiency is missed.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 22/04 s. 8: construction inspected and certified safe before it is put into use

evidence.note: Inspection share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Energize and release protection
steps.description: The crew removes grounds and tags and surrenders the permit. The system operator switches the section into service, restores the normal open point and confirms customers are back on.

error.defect_description: Normal open point not updated in the outage system.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code (IHSA): work protection permit and tags issued by the control room before work on isolated plant

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Clean up and return equipment
steps.description: The crew closes vaults, returns empty reels and removed transformers to the yard (old units go for PCB testing and disposal), credits unused material and reports truck defects.

error.defect_description: Removed transformer not recorded for disposal.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the work order and redlines
steps.description: The crew lead records splice locations, cable lengths and equipment serial numbers on the drawing, enters crew hours by work order and completes the job in the mobile tool.

error.defect_description: Splice location or serial number missing, or hours on the wrong order.

evidence.note: Error rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and sign off the job
steps.description: The underground supervisor reviews hours, redlines and test records, approves the timesheets and signs the job complete, or returns it to the crew lead for missing information.

error.defect_description: A wrong charge is approved.

control.basis: Collective agreement and payroll policy: supervisor approval of crew time

evidence.note: Return rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the field work order and send the as-built
steps.description: The work planner sets the field work order to complete in the ERP, scans redlines and test records into the document repository and sends the as-built package to the capital project manager.

error.defect_description: Scan missing or attached to the wrong job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Civil work not ready
exceptions.description: Ducts, vaults or pads are unfinished or deficient; the job waits for the contractor and the inspector rechecks.

exceptions.name: Long-lead equipment on backorder
exceptions.description: A padmount transformer, switchgear or cable is not in stock; the job slips until delivery.

exceptions.name: Outage moved
exceptions.description: A customer asks to move the outage, the crew is pulled to a cable fault, or frost stops excavation; switching and notices are rebooked.

exceptions.name: Failed cable test
exceptions.description: The new section fails its test and a splice or termination is redone before energizing.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from job release to the crew to as-built handed to the project manager
benchmarks.population: Ontario municipal distributor in-house underground jobs, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: civil readiness and ten-business-day multi-address locates, outage notice lead time, the crew day, then one to two weeks of close-out; contractor delays drive the tail.
More than 90% XLPE, much of it installed from the mid-1970s to 1990 and at or past its 30-year expected life.

pain_points.description: Crews arrive to find ducts or pads unfinished or blocked; civil readiness depends on contractors outside the crew's control.

evidence.note: Contractor-built civil works (source); frequency is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Multi-address locates take up to ten business days and outages need advance customer notice, so preparation takes weeks for a one or two day crew job.
Padmount transformer and switchgear lead times stretched in 2021-2022, stalling staged jobs.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Splice locations and serial numbers are captured on paper or tablet redlines and often come back incomplete, delaying records.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: Fortune Cable Renewal
sources.supports: Cable renewal done by Hydro Ottawa crews and contractors: buried ducts and concrete-encased road crossings, cable and transformer replacement (46 and 30 transformers in two phases), multi-phase over two years, temporary backfill then reinstatement when weather allows.

sources.title: An in-depth look at Hydro Ottawa's grid maintenance
sources.supports: Critical pole program tests thousands of poles a year; replacements are driven by testing or by emergencies such as vehicle collisions; cable replacements are prioritised from fault histories, cable tests and estimated life; new cable goes in 4-inch PVC or HDPE conduit.

sources.title: Contractors: locates and safe digging
sources.supports: Locate requests at least five business days before digging (ten for multi-address requests), legally required; hand digging or hydrovac near cables; stay 1.5 m from marked cables; re-locate when marks expire. Current page; the five-business-day rule applied in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Regulation Technical Guidelines (Ontario Regulation 22/04)
sources.supports: Ontario Regulation 22/04: all equipment and plans or standard design drawings must be approved (ss. 6-7); all construction inspected and certified safe before use (s. 8); annual audit of compliance; serious electrical incidents reported to ESA within 48 hours.

sources.title: Keys to the Utility Work Protection Code
sources.publisher: Infrastructure Health and Safety Association (IHSA) Health and Safety Magazine, vol. 23 issue 2
sources.supports: The Electrical Utility Safety Rules govern worker conduct near hazards; the Utility Work Protection Code uses permits and tags to show when lines are safe to work on; issuers and workers must be trained and certified.

sources.title: Wages: Lineworker - Electrical Power Systems in Ontario (NOC 72203)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wage low 29.70, median 49.48, high 62.90; Ottawa region 32.93, 50.63, 63.29 (2024-2025 reference period).

sources.title: Utility Proactively Tests Underground Cable (Alana Jones and Bill Bennett)
sources.supports: Hydro Ottawa has nearly 5,000 km of underground cable, more than 90% XLPE, much installed from the mid-1970s to 1990 and at or past its 30-year expected life; replacing on faults is a lagging approach; injection versus replacement depends on splice count and feasibility.

assumptions: The process starts when work scheduling releases the job to a cable crew and ends when the as-built reaches the capital project manager; civil construction, design, switching and GIS posting are other processes.
Crew work is recorded as elapsed crew time with people = 3 (or 2 splicers plus a concurrent apprentice step for splicing).
About 70% of jobs include a cable pull and about half set or replace padmount equipment; every job ties into the energized system under a work protection permit.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
The digger derrick stands in for the boom truck used to lift padmount transformers.
